Positive earnings surprises and stock-price reactions

A beat is not a direction signal. Separate the overnight gap, the reaction session, and the trade that is still available after the release.

Prepared October 22, 2026. MySQL 8.0 jstockdata_curr prices: 2024-01-02 through 2026-10-16. Current trades need newer prices.

Coverage

5,547 earnings rows across 499 symbols. 499 symbols are classified as stocks using jstockdata_scrips plus Yahoo EQUITY verification for missing master records; 0 non-stock or unclassified symbols excluded. 5,433 events have an exact report-date bar plus both adjacent market sessions; 4,423 are positive surprises. 4,409 positive events remain after price-quality flags.

Supplementary Yahoo equity classifications: ADP, APP, BNY, EQIX, FCX, MCK, PSX, PWR, SYK, TT, VRT. These were missing from the local master, not excluded as ETFs.

Report focuses on positive surprises. Pre-release risk uses all available surprises, including zero/negative values. Existing holdings are not evaluated for valuation, taxes, or portfolio suitability.

All stock summaries and trade approaches · Event calculations and source OHLC · Excluded-event audit

PG and AAPL: the timing check

Yahoo timestamps identify PG as before-market and AAPL as after-market for the matched study events. PG's reaction uses the report session; AAPL's uses the next session. Times are provider evidence, not independently verified for every release. Same-day returns for AAPL generally precede its announcement.

PG 11 63.64 0.54 45.45 -0.49 63.64 0.54 0.70

PG rose on 7 of 11 reaction sessions, but its median open-to-close return was approximately −0.05%: much of the gain was already in the opening gap. AAPL rose in 8 of 11 later five-session windows, but after a negative initial reaction only 4 of 7 rose (median +0.50%); after a positive initial reaction 4 of 4 rose (median +5.92%). These tiny conditional samples do not establish a buy-the-dip rule.

See the expanded PG and AAPL event tables below. Positive EPS can coexist with falling prices because guidance, revenue, margins, positioning and expectations beyond the published consensus also matter. This dataset does not identify which factor caused an individual move.

How to use the three trading stages

  1. Before the release: never condition an entry on a future realized beat. Default to waiting. A bullish thesis can use a bull call debit spread; a bearish thesis can use a bear put debit spread. Debit paid is the planned maximum loss. Directional credit spreads require enough premium and a defensible support/resistance level. Historical move size alone does not establish positive option expectancy.
  2. On earnings / the reaction session: for BMO, use that day's open; for AMC, use the following trading session. Wait for the first 30-minute range. Consider continuation above its high with VWAP support (long) or below its low with VWAP resistance (bearish). A gap-fade needs a failed range break and a VWAP reversal, with the previous close as a possible target. The OHLC table cannot test these intraday triggers. Skip if spread/slippage is excessive.
  3. Carry afterward: review the position at D+1 close; a common timing-safe proxy enters at D+2 open and exits D+6 close (five trading sessions). Carry only if the observed price trend supports the direction. Exit on a break of the reaction structure or at the time limit; overnight stops can slip. Bull put spreads fit bullish support; bear call spreads fit bearish resistance, conditional on actual quotes. For illustration, cap maximum loss at 0.25%–0.5% of account equity per idea, sized from the stop or spread maximum loss, not share count.

Iron butterfly: not recommended automatically before earnings. A short iron butterfly sells an ATM call and put and buys farther OTM wings; its small profit zone can be overwhelmed by an event gap. Consider only with verified release timing, liquid options, a defensible implied-versus-realized-move advantage, and a tolerable wing-width-minus-credit maximum loss. An iron condor offers a wider neutral range. After earnings, IV compression may already have removed most of the credit; low realized movement is not enough to justify either structure. Plan to close short spreads before expiration to manage assignment and pin risk.

Definitions and limits

  • D is the reported date; D+1 is the next actual SPY market session. Same-day = close(D)/close(D−1)−1. Next-day = close(D+1)/close(D)−1. Two-session = close(D+1)/close(D−1)−1. Gaps use open/prior close. All returns shown in percentage points, e.g. 2.00 means 2%.
  • For all stocks except PG/AAPL, release times are unavailable. The two-session window captures either BMO or AMC but also includes a non-reaction session. It must not be called an executable earnings-day return. Report-date holidays/weekends and missing adjacent bars are excluded, not shifted automatically.
  • Carry = close(D+6)/open(D+2)−1, before fees, spreads and slippage. This is a fixed-horizon long-equity proxy on positive-surprise events, not a backtest of the suggested opening-range or options strategies.
  • Current-table OHLC adjustment status is not documented. Events with a daily close move or opening gap over 30% are flagged and excluded from summary estimation pending corporate-action review; raw records remain in the event CSV. This can remove genuine tail moves, so affected stocks receive no strategy selection. Carry windows with daily close moves over 30% are separately flagged. Smaller split/dividend effects may remain. No total-return adjustment is assumed.
  • Exact duplicate input rows removed: 0. Conflicting same-symbol/date records are excluded. Nonpositive includes zero and negative surprise, not missing surprise. Blank metrics mean unavailable.
  • Profiles are exploratory rules: at least 8 usable total events and 6 beats; bullish/bearish watch requires two-session up frequency ≥70%/≤30% and median ≥0.5%/≤−0.5%. Other stocks are mixed. Carry uses the same 70%/30% and ±0.5% thresholds with at least 6 observations. Pre-release neutral screening requires an all-event 90th-percentile absolute move ≤4% and up frequency between 35% and 65%; ≥8% move triggers large-event-risk guidance. These are research cutoffs, not optimized or validated edges.
  • Samples cover fewer than three years and often only a handful of quarters. Wilson intervals assume independent events and are descriptive. No multiple-testing correction, out-of-sample validation, historical option chains, IV, execution costs, or intraday bars are available. Current-universe survivorship and historical vendor revisions can bias the study. SPY excess is a simple paired return difference, not beta-adjusted alpha.

Exclusion counts: {"missing_date_or_surprise": 5, "outside_price_coverage_or_nontrading_date": 96, "missing_adjacent_price_bar": 11, "conflicting_duplicate_date": 2}.

Before earnings
Prefer no new pre-release position: fewer than two observed nonpositive surprises, so miss risk is not calibrated. If independently bullish/bearish, a small debit spread caps loss; avoid an automatic earnings iron butterfly.

On the reaction session
Use the next session after the after-close release. A beat alone is not a buy: reduce equity or use a bear put spread only on a confirmed opening-range breakdown; buy only on a confirmed reclaim.

Carry after earnings
Conditional long carry after D+1 strength: equity or bull call spread with support intact. Overall 8/11 five-session windows rose, but only 4/7 after a negative reaction; do not mechanically buy the dip. Bull put spread requires adequate premium.
